Write a short blog post about the value of owning a home. Aim for about 400 words. Reply with the post only.
final_message:
The Value of Owning a Home

There is no lesson that I wish more young people would learn than this one: that the man or woman who owns a home has laid hold of something far more valuable than a house and a piece of ground. He has laid hold of a foundation upon which a useful life can be built.

Let us consider, first, what it means in the matter of money. The person who pays rent, year after year, has at the end of the time nothing to show for it but a handful of receipts. The person who pays for a home, even if it be a small and plain one, finds that every payment adds something to his own possessions. It is a kind of saving that does not depend upon one's being in the mood to save. The payment must be made, and so it is made, and the habit of thrift is formed almost without one's knowing it. I have seen many a family that could never have laid by a dollar in any other way, become possessed of a comfortable property by this simple plan.

But the value of a home is not to be measured in dollars alone. The man who owns his home takes a new interest in everything about him. He mends the fence, he plants the tree, he keeps the walk in order, and he does these things, not because anyone has commanded him, but because the place is his own. He becomes interested in good roads, in good schools, in good government, since he knows that the worth of his property depends upon the character of the community in which it stands. In this way, the home-owner becomes, almost without trying, a better citizen.

Then, too, there is the effect upon the children. A child who grows up in a home that belongs to his father and mother learns to feel that he has a place in the world, a place that is secure, and that cannot be taken from him at the whim of another. He learns to take care of what is his. He learns that things worth having are worth working for. These are lessons that no school can teach so well as a home can teach them.

I do not say that every one can buy a home tomorrow. I do say that every one can make up his mind that he is going to have one, and that he will go forward, in a patient and humble way, saving a little here and a little there, until the day comes when he can say, "This is mine." That day, I think you will find, is worth all the waiting and all the effort that it costs.
